the optimisation of the RT step in qRT-PCR when using FFPE derived RNA.

In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the use of a reduced RNaseH RT enzyme is a key factor when using FFPE prostate tissue RNA as a template for gene expression analysis.
the use of a reduced RNaseH RT is recommended when using FFPE derived RNA for qRT-PCR applications.
the choice of RT enzyme is critical when using FFPE samples.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of the Superscript III RT with RNaseH- (Invitrogen) is recommended when using FFPE derived RNA.
the use of a M-MLV Reverse Transcriptase with reduced RNasesH activity is recommended when using FFPE derived RNA for gene expression analysis.
FFPE RNA can be used in gene expression studies, however it is important to consider the RNA isolation method and RT enzyme used.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the choice of RNA isolation method and reverse transcriptase is crucial when using formalin fixed paraffin embedded RNA as a template and can affect the outcome and sensitivity of PCR applications.
when using FFPE tissue, the choice of RT can significantly affect the outcome of gene expression studies.
the use of an M-MVL RT with reduced RNase H activity can increase the sensitivity and reproducibility of gene expression analysis in FFPE samples.
